provenance.post_check: reviewer-name tokens replaced by [name] after the quote check

issues.text: No statistical power calculation is provided for the analysis, and the evaluator asks the authors to comment on or include statistical power given its absence from the paper.
issues.quote: Statistical power calculation[s were] not provided.

issues.text: The literature review is one-sided: it cites many studies of deworming with positive findings but few critical ones, so the evaluator suggests citing more critical papers to give a more balanced view.
issues.quote: There are several studies analysing impacts of deworming mentioned, although all on the more 'positive' side.

issues.text: Summary statistics for the covariates discussed on page 6 are not provided, making it harder for readers to assess them; the evaluator requests a table in the online additional exhibits.
issues.quote: It would be helpful to the reader if the authors include a table in the additional exhibits (for online publication) with summary statistics for the covariates discussed in page 6.

issues.text: In the channels analysis (Table 2), the number of observations varies across outcomes, so the evaluator questions whether the results are robust when the sample is held constant across specifications.
issues.quote: The number of observations changes for each outcome. Are results robust to keeping the same observations across all specifications?

issues.text: The claimed dose-response relationship is not convincingly supported by Figure 2: the two-year bins appear to group 0 and 1-2 together and 3-4 and 5-6 together, which suggests no monotonic dose-response, and the evaluator questions whether hypothesis testing is provided.
issues.quote: it looks more like 0 and 1-2 being together (same) VS 3-4 and 5-6 being together (same), i.e. no dose-response.

issues.text: The paper does not examine birth outcomes (such as birth weight or gestational age) or sex ratio at birth as a proxy for fetal loss, which the evaluator considers interesting if the data contain them.
issues.quote: It would be interesting to see if there are any effects on birth outcomes, such as birth weight [or] gestational age

issues.text: Other health outcomes measured at or before age 5, such as height or stunting, are not analysed, though the evaluator suggests they may be available in the data.
issues.quote: Are there any other health outcomes measured at (or before) age 5? Height, for example, to examine stunting?

issues.text: The evaluator suggests comparing outcomes between parents and children and how the intervention affects their correlation, contingent on data availability; this is presented as a possible extension.
issues.quote: it would be interesting to compare same outcomes for parents and their children and the impact of the intervention on their correlation.

issues.text: Heterogeneous results by parents' age are placed in the appendix, though the evaluator finds them valuable and suggests moving some to the main text with further discussion; Table A.6 is also not mentioned in the text.
issues.quote: Also, Table A.6 is not mentioned anywhere in the text

issues.text: The discussion of Duhon et al. (2023) covers non-/cognitive gains but gives little discussion of the health gains examined in that study, which the evaluator considers useful for readers.
issues.quote: a brief discussion of the health gains examined in that study would be beneficial for the reader.

issues.text: The paper lacks discussion or direct comparison with Barham et al. (2023) in Bangladesh, which the evaluator considers the study most closely related to this one.
issues.quote: I think the authors would assist the reader by providing discussion (or direct comparison when possible) of the study of Barham et al.

issues.text: Some results in the tables are not discussed in the main text, and some typical outcomes are neither present nor mentioned, which the evaluator considers a gap in the analysis.
issues.quote: Some results in tables could be discussed further in [the] text. Some typical outcomes [were] not present (nor mentioned)
